quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: The Strait of Juan de Fuca, which you can see from Port Angeles, was named after a Greek sailor who sailed for Spain in 1592. He claimed to have found the waterway connecting the Pacific Ocean to the Atlantic—though this Northwest Passage didn't actually exist, his name stuck to this beautiful strait!

short_read.title: How Plants Know When It's Time to Bloom
short_read.teaser: Scientists have discovered that plants can actually measure day length using special proteins that act like tiny clocks. It's nature's way of making sure flowers appear at just the right time of year!

medium_read.title: The Secret Lives of Harbor Seals in the Pacific Northwest
medium_read.teaser: Harbor seals are year-round residents of the waters around Port Angeles, and they're much more intelligent and social than most people realize. Learn about their family bonds, communication skills, and how they navigate the cold waters of the Strait.

long_read.title: The Flavors of Hungary: A Culinary Journey
long_read.teaser: From paprika-laden stews to delicate pastries, Hungarian cuisine tells the story of a nation at the crossroads of empires. This beautiful exploration celebrates the dishes, traditions, and family memories that make Hungarian food so special.

port_angeles.title: Eagle Migration Season on the Peninsula
port_angeles.description: September is prime time for watching bald eagles along the Dungeness Spit and Ediz Hook! These majestic birds gather to feed on salmon returning to spawn. Early morning and late afternoon offer the best viewing opportunities as eagles soar above the water hunting for fish.

puzzle_1.question: A bald eagle's nest, called an eyrie, can weigh up to ___ pounds—about as much as a small car!
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right! Those eagle nests are incredibly massive—built year after year until they become enormous structures!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! The answer is 2,000 pounds—these nests can truly become gigantic over the years!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: The answer is 2,000 pounds! Hard to imagine, isn't it? Eagles add to their nests year after year, making them some of the largest nests in the bird world.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Bald eagles return to the same nest each year, adding more sticks and branches. The largest recorded bald eagle nest was in Florida—it measured 9.5 feet wide and 20 feet deep!

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'hello' or 'goodbye'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Perfect! Szia (pronounced 'see-ah') is such a friendly, casual way to greet someone or say goodbye in Hungarian!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'Szia' (pronounced 'see-ah')! It's a casual, warm way to say both hello and goodbye. Köszönöm means 'thank you,' Szeretlek means 'I love you,' and Viszlát is a more formal 'goodbye.'
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is part of the Finno-Ugric language family, making it quite unique in Europe. It's most closely related to Finnish and Estonian, though even those languages are quite different!

puzzle_3.question: What amazing ability do hummingbirds have that no other birds can do?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Yes! Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards—and they can also hover in place like tiny helicopters. Their wings beat up to 80 times per second!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The answer is fly backwards! Hummingbirds are the only birds with this special ability. Their unique wing structure lets them fly backwards, forwards, and even hover perfectly still in the air.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Hummingbirds have incredible metabolism—their hearts can beat over 1,200 times per minute! Anna's hummingbirds are common visitors to gardens in Port Angeles year-round.
